new_entities.name: Maxillomandibular advancement for obstructive sleep apnea
new_entities.description: Maxillomandibular advancement surgery used to enlarge the pharyngeal airway in obstructive sleep apnea.

new_entities.name: Reduction in apnea-hypopnea index
new_entities.description: A reduction in the apnea-hypopnea index, indicating fewer obstructive breathing events during sleep.

edges.effect_quant: Maxillomandibular advancement has one of the largest surgical effects on OSA severity. A 2025 meta-analysis found pooled AHI improvement of -41.87 events/h, while cohort series reported 83% mean AHI reduction and 100% surgical success in selected patients at follow-up.
edges.population: adults with moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea selected for definitive airway-enlarging surgery, often after CPAP intolerance or craniofacial risk factors
edges.mechanism: Advancing the maxilla and mandible enlarges the retropalatal and retrolingual airway, tensions surrounding soft tissues, and reduces airway collapsibility across multiple levels.
edges.summary: This is one of the strongest procedural edges in the whole sleep-apnea block. When patients are appropriately selected, MMA can produce large and durable objective improvements in OSA severity.
edges.caveats: It is major surgery with postoperative morbidity and neurosensory sequelae, and most evidence comes from single-arm series rather than sham-controlled trials. Selection bias likely inflates some reported success rates.

evidence.citation: WalkerA et al 2025 Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg
evidence.notes: Maxillomandibular Advancement Safety and Effectiveness in Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

evidence.citation: VargheseR et al 2012 Int J Otolaryngol
evidence.notes: Maxillomandibular advancement in the management of obstructive sleep apnea.

effect_quant.comparator: Group mean AHI reduction about 6.7 months after maxillomandibular advancement
